title: spec review: Q3 v2: orchestrator/planner_packet.py — compact, delta-oriented Planner decision packets and the escalation packet (Planner respawn after T-0695 returned non-JSON)
spec: Review the spec of execute task T-0689 (inputs[0]) before any code is written: risks, suggested_spec_changes, verdict approve|request_changes. planner_taxonomy.py (T-0675) is merged on goal/T-0674 and defines DECISION_TYPES and classify(); scout_evidence.normalize_findings returns entries keyed finding/source/confidence/relevance/unresolved/needs_challenge. Reply with exactly one JSON object, no prose.
acceptance: result carries verdict approve or request_changes with risks and suggested_spec_changes

risks.issue: The truncation algorithm only ever drops whole named sections (Memory, Scout findings, Unresolved alternatives, Changes, then failures text within Relevant task state) but defines no final hard backstop (the existing decision_packet() always does `text[:cap]`). With many sections or long untruncated fields (task title, hold_reason, status, depends_on statuses are never capped per-section), build() can still emit text over cap_chars after exhausting the cut list, and the acceptance test for cap 1200 only checks cut order/protected sections, not that len(text) <= cap. Since this packet is fed straight into a paid headless Planner call, an unbounded prompt is exactly the kind of unguarded-external-call risk this module exists to prevent.

build()'s behavior when previous is given but changes is None (or omitted) is unspecified: section 3 is defined only for previous=None (fixed sentence) and for previous+changes together (line list + previous['state_version']). A caller that passes previous without changes — a normal case, since a caller may know the goal changed but not have a diff — is left to guess, and a naive implementation indexing previous['state_version'] will KeyError if state_version is absent instead of using .get().

suggested_spec_changes: Specify a final hard truncation step in build() (e.g. `text = text[:cap_chars]` after section-level cuts, mirroring planner_runs.decision_packet's existing `[:cap]` backstop), and add an acceptance assertion that len(result['text']) <= cap_chars even in the cap:1200/long-failures case.

Define section 3's rendering when previous is given but changes is None/omitted (e.g. 'state changed since previous decision, no field-level diff available' plus previous.get('state_version')), and add an acceptance case for that combination so implementers don't have to guess.
